title.big: Rig capability screen, via engineering conversation
title.desc: Describe the field program in plain English. Deckhand asks for what drives the rig, screens the fleet against it, and sends back a ranked shortlist you can take into sourcing.

turns.html: We're locking the rig strategy for a Cape-style geothermal field — multi-well pads, long laterals, hot hard rock. Before I go out to the drillers, can you screen the usual onshore super-spec rigs and tell me which actually fit?

Happy to screen them. Two things set the bar, so let me get them straight first:
  • Well-design envelope — target TVD, measured depth and lateral length, plus the heaviest string you'll hang. That drives the hookload gate and the mud-pressure I have to see.
  • What you're optimising — every super-spec rig clears the basics, so the ranking comes down to weights: pad mobility, automation/data, power & emissions, and high-temperature track record. Geothermal usually pushes HT readiness up.
I'll gate on the super-spec floor (AC drive, ≥1,500 HP, ≥750k lb hookload, 7,500 psi, walking) and rank whoever clears it.
Public rig-class specs only — marketing-grade, not contractual. The binding number is the per-rig IADC daily report.

8,600 m… sorry, 8,600 ft TVD, 11,000 ft MD, 5,000 ft lateral. Heaviest string ~600k lb, mud to 7,500 psi, bottomhole ~400 °F, crystalline basement. 12-well pads. Weight HT readiness highest, then pad mobility. Candidates and the program are in the file.

Got it — 600k lb string × 1.25 design factor stays under the 750k super-spec floor, so the hookload gate holds at 750k lb. HT readiness weighted highest, then pad mobility, with automation/data and power behind. Screening five candidate rigs against the gate, then ranking the survivors. Running it now…

Here's the screen — 4 of 5 clear the gate, one is knocked out:
RankRigFitVerdict
1FlexRig — HT pack0.70✅ Qualified
2H&P FlexRig0.65✅ Qualified
3Patterson APEX XC0.65✅ Qualified
4Precision ST-15000.63✅ Qualified
—Nabors PACE-X800—❌ Disqualified
PACE-X800 fails one hard gate: pad capability skidding ≠ walking — it uses an X-Y skid, not omnidirectional walking, so it can't factory-drill your 12-well pads. The HT-pack FlexRig tops the list because you weighted high-temperature readiness highest; every score traces back to a cited spec.

closing.headline: Rig capability screen: super-spec gate + weighted fit, ranked for field development.
